ocf.heading: Cash Flows from Operating Activities
ocf.text:
During the six months ended June 27, 2026, net cash provided by operating activities was primarily attributable to (i) consolidated net income of $491.7 million and (ii) an increase in current liabilities of $167.9 million. There were also increases due to non-cash adjustments primarily consisting of (i) depreciation and amortization of $34.0 million and (ii) stock-based compensation expense of $15.8 million. These increases were partially offset by (i) an increase in accounts receivable of $292.2 million, (ii) an increase in inventories of $89.2 million, and (iii) a gain of $41.4 million related to the sale of the Sherwood business.

During the six months ended June 28, 2025, net cash provided by operating activities was primarily attributable to (i) consolidated net income of $407.8 million, (ii) an increase in current liabilities of $72.3 million, and (iii) non-capital related insurance proceeds of $12.3 million for the March 2023 tornado in Covington, Tennessee. There were also increases due to non-cash adjustments primarily consisting of (i) depreciation and amortization of $35.0 million and (ii) stock-based compensation expense of $13.9 million.

da.text: Cost of goods sold increased in the second quarter of 2026 primarily due to the factors noted above regarding the change in net sales. Gross margin as a percentage of sales was 27.7 percent compared with 31.0 percent in the prior year quarter. Depreciation and amortization was consistent with the second quarter of 2025. Selling, general, and administrative expense increased slightly in the second quarter of 2026 primarily as a result of (i) higher employment costs, including incentive compensation, of $1.6 million, (ii) higher legal and professional fees of $1.5 million, and (iii) incremental expenses of $1.4 million associated with Bison. These increases were largely offset by (i) lower product-related costs of $1.4 million, (ii) lower foreign currency transaction losses of $1.2 million, (iii) the absence of $0.5 million of expenses associated with Sherwood, and (iv) lower taxes and insurance of $0.4 million. In addition, during the second quarter of 2025, we recognized a gain of $36.3 million for the excess of insurance proceeds received over the losses incurred related to the March 2023 tornado at our Covington, Tennessee manufacturing operation.

wc.text: We believe that cash provided by operations, funds available under the Credit Agreement, and cash on hand will be adequate to meet our liquidity needs, including working capital, capital expenditures, and debt payment obligations.

capex.text: The major components of net cash used in investing activities during the six months ended June 27, 2026 included (i) $138.3 million for the purchase of Bison and (ii) capital expenditures of $38.8 million. These uses were partially offset by proceeds from the sale of the Sherwood business, net of cash sold, of $57.0 million.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
